result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A turns every session point into a realistic floor scenario. Its wrong options are tempting, like a test lift on a slightly overweight pallet or wiping up a small leak, and every option gets feedback explaining why it's right or wrong. Answer B covers all the topics too, but mostly asks learners to recite numbers and rules. Several of its wrong options are filler ('It doesn't matter', 'Sideways', 'break room manual'), and its key gives almost no explanation. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B sets every question on the warehouse floor, gives believable wrong options (a test lift, forks at the right height but the mast upright, reversing with the forks downhill) and explains each one, and it covers every topic in the session. Answer A mostly asks people to recite rules and numbers, has filler options like 'It doesn't matter' and 'Speed up to clear it quickly', and explains almost nothing. B does add some reasons not in the list (overloaded forklifts tip, forks at floor level can catch), but these explain the rules rather than add new ones.
